Phase 1 - Establish temporary camp

I would hang a tarp (included in survival pack) over the tent suspended from the trees around me for even more protection from the element. This would serve as my base of operations while I began preparing Phase II.

Phase II - Build permanent home

In this phase I would build a permanent home, in the trees. Complete with Indoor plumbing, water tank heated by the sun, elevator (rope and pully system) to get supplies up to house, waste disposal system (that doubled as a Compost bin). Also I would build (at ground level near house) a building to hold my stove (built from baked mud bricks). The chimney of the stove would go straight up (above my house in the trees) with a damper that when closed would redirect the heated exhaust through baked mud pipes in the walls of my house (heating) and then exhaust out the roof of the house.

Phase III - Manufacturing

In this phase I would use the laptop/tablet (and its reference materials) to scavenge/mine for raw materials to make additional items with. At first I would focus on scavenging metals, metal them down and use a machine I built to spin the melted metal into thin wire (like hair thickness). Once I had enough wire I would scavenge for Natural Earth Magnets (if I couldn't find any I make my own) and use the magnets and wire to build a Wind Turbine that I would erect on the highest (windiest) part of the island. I would then make more wire (thicker to carry the electricity from turbine) and connect the power from the turbine to my house. Underneath my house I would build tanks (from baked mud) to hold seawater and build Seawater Batteries to store the electricity from the Wind Turbine. Now that I have electricity I would figure out how to blow glass to make things like Light Bulbs so I can see in my house at night. Then I would start building my own massive solar panels from materials I scavenged/mined so when there is no wind I still have power.

Phase IV - Improvements

In this phase I would focus on improving everything I have already built. I would start by building a large kiln to bake large amounts of bricks at one time. I would make and store enough bricks to build a full house out of brick. Once I had enough Brick built and stored I would clear an area of land and build a new house out of 95% brick. With the floor, walls and roof all being made from brick. I would then use my glass making/blowing furnace to make windows and put them in my new house. The new house would have a stove (and heat) built in and would much cooler in the summer and warmer in the winter. Next I would build better and more efficient batteries. By mining, refining materials and developing chemicals (from plants and minerals) I would build a massive power storage facility with far more efficient energy storage so I never run out of power. Then I would build larger and more powerful Wind Turbines and Solar Cells to keep those batteries fully charged year round.

Phase V - Manufacturing 2.0

By this point my mining and manufacturing has become limited. I would now focus on developing the tools, machines, etc. needed to manufacture semiconductors (chips) and other electronic components like Resisters, diodes, capacitors, etc. I would achieve this by building a 3d printer that can print (simultaneously) in multiple materials like metal, plastic, silicon, etc. Once I have a building built (brick) to house my new 3d printers I would stockpile (manufacture) large amounts of the materials I would need to manufacture machines, computers, radios, displays, etc.

Phase VI - Next level computing

Now that I can manufacture all the components needed to build computers that is exactly what I would do. At best the first computers would be along the lines of the 486 levels of power. So I would build dozens of them, networked together running a version of DSL (Damn Small Linux) that I had stored on my laptop/tablet. I would then use the 2nd gen super computer to design and build the 3rd gen super computer (think current computing/storage capabilities). The 3rd gen super computer would keep getting expanded until there where 1024 networked computers. I now have the computing power and storage capacity for anything I want to design/build. All the information on my tablet/laptop has multiple backups across the 3rd gen super computer array.

Phase VII - Quality of Life

By this point I have read all the books, watched all the TV shows and movies and am downright bored....what to do? I know I will build a humanoid companion. A robot that looks and feels human. This robot will have an internal battery and WiFi/Bluetooth connection to the super computer. When it "sleeps" it will wirelessly recharge its battery. Along with the humanoid robot I will design a rudimentary AI that runs on the super computer. This AI will be capable of learning from the world around it, from me and from all the materials and knowledge I brought with me on the laptop/tablet. As we interact it will become more and more human and offer the stimulation needed to keep me happy and healthy.
